Table 1: Comparison of existing methods against PAMF. Methods include MulT [41], TFN [52], MAG [31], FuseMoE [11], FlexMoE [51], Maestro [28], MIRA [18], and representative singlemodality imputation models such as CSDI [39] and SSSD [26]. Imp.: explicit reconstruction; E2E: imputation and fusion trained end-to-end.

Table 2: Classification performance on four benchmarks under 20% missingness, with withinmodality missing and modality-level missing evaluated separately. Means and standard deviations over three runs are rounded to three decimals. Bold: best; underlined: second-best.

Table 8: Exact HPO values used in Figure 2 on PTB-XL under mixed 20% missingness. The exploratory N=1 point is omitted to match the plotted figure. Means and standard deviations are reported exactly from the paper-facing plotting source.

Table 9: Clean-input classification performance on the three benchmarks with complete clean summaries in the current archive. To match the main-paper comparison set, the table reports the same primary baselines and excludes ShaSpec and CLIMB. Means and standard deviations over three runs are rounded to three decimals. Bold: best; underlined: second-best within the reported comparison set.
Figure 2: Hyperparameter sensitivity of our encoder configuration on PTB-XL under mixed 20% missingness. Left: sweep over the number of experts N . Right: sweep over the expert size dmodal.

Figure 1: Overview of PAMF. Left: the end-to-end pipeline combines an imputation encoder himp, a fusion encoder hfus, a flow matching module ffm, and a downstream head fds. himp extracts the imputation context cimp from the observed inputs. Conditioned on cimp and a prior-aware source state x0, ffm imputes the missing signals to generate completed data, which are then fed into hfus to produce the fused representation cfus for downstream head fds to predict y. Right: the shared MoE encoder backbone used by both encoders.
